notes.title: Introduction to C – revision sheet
notes.md:
## History
- BCPL (Martin Richards, 1967) → B (Ken Thompson, 1970) → **C (Dennis Ritchie, AT&T Bell Labs, 1972)**, written for UNIX
- K&R C (Kernighan & Ritchie book, 1978); ANSI C89 / ISO C90; C99 (// comments, long long, bool); C11; C17
- Middle-level language: high-level constructs + pointers, bit operations; portable; compiled; case-sensitive

## Structure of a C program
1. Documentation (comments `/* … */`)  2. Link section (`#include <stdio.h>`)  3. Definition (`#define PI 3.14`)
4. Global declarations  5. `main()` – execution starts here (exactly one)  6. User-defined functions
- Every statement ends with `;`; `return 0;` = success
- Build: preprocess (.i) → compile (.s) → assemble (.o/.obj) → link (.exe/a.out)

## Character set and tokens
- Letters, digits, special characters, white space (not in basic set: `$ @ \``)
- Escape sequences: `\n` newline, `\t` tab, `\b` backspace, `\r` carriage return, `\0` null, `\\` backslash, `\'`, `\"`
- Tokens: keywords (32 in C89), identifiers, constants, strings, operators, special symbols

## Constants, variables, data types
- Primary constants: integer (`-275`, `010` octal = 8, `0x1F` = 31), real (`3.2e-5`, type double), character (`'A'` = 65)
- Secondary: arrays, pointers, structures, unions, enums
- Identifiers: letters, digits, `_`; not starting with a digit; not a keyword; case-sensitive
- Sizes (typical 32-bit): char 1, short 2, int 4 (Turbo C: 2 → −32768…32767), long 4/8, float 4, double 8
- signed char −128…127; unsigned char 0…255; `sizeof('A')` = sizeof(int) in C
- Format specifiers: %d %i int, %u unsigned, %ld long, %f float/double (printf), %lf double (scanf), %c char, %s string, %o octal, %x hex, %e, %p pointer
- Constants: `const int N = 10;` or `#define N 10`; `void` = no value

notes.title: Introduction to C – detailed notes with worked examples
notes.md:
## History in one line
BCPL (Martin Richards, 1967) → B (Ken Thompson, 1970) → **C (Dennis Ritchie, Bell Labs, 1972)**, written to re-implement **UNIX**.
Standards: K&R C (1978 book) → **ANSI C / C89** (= ISO C90) → C99 → C11 → C17 → C23. C is a **middle-level, procedural, structured** language.

## Structure of a C program
```c
/* 1. documentation section */
#include <stdio.h>        /* 2. link section            */
#define PI 3.14159        /* 3. definition section      */
int count = 0;            /* 4. global declarations     */
int area(int r);          /*    function prototypes     */
int main(void)            /* 5. main() – execution starts here */
{
    printf("%d\n", area(2));
    return 0;             /* 0 = success to the OS      */
}
int area(int r) { return PI * r * r; }   /* 6. sub-programs */
```
Output: `12` – 3.14159 × 4 = 12.566…, converted to int on return (truncated, not rounded).

## From source to running program
`prog.c` → **preprocessor** (`prog.i`: includes pasted, macros expanded, comments removed) → **compiler** (`prog.s`, assembly) → **assembler** (`prog.o` / `.obj`, object code) → **linker** (+ library code → `a.out` / `prog.exe`) → **loader** puts it in memory.
- Syntax errors come from the compiler; "undefined reference to …" comes from the **linker**; division by zero shows up only at **run time**.

## Character set, tokens, keywords, identifiers
- Tokens: keywords, identifiers, constants, string literals, operators, punctuators (`; , { } ( ) [ ]`)
- **32 keywords in C89**: auto break case char const continue default do double else enum extern float for goto if int long register return short signed sizeof static struct switch typedef union unsigned void volatile while. C99 added inline, restrict, _Bool, _Complex, _Imaginary.
- Identifier rules: letters, digits, `_`; must not start with a digit; case-sensitive; not a keyword
  - Valid: `_sum`, `total1`, `Int`, `__x` · Invalid: `1total`, `int`, `my-var`, `my var`, `rate%`
- `main`, `printf`, `scanf` are **not** keywords (they are identifiers).

## Constants and data types
| Constant | Example | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Decimal / octal / hex integer | `25`, `031`, `0x19` | all = 25 |
| Real | `3.14`, `2.5e3` | 2500.0 |
| Character | `'A'` | 65 (type int in C) |
| String | `"A"` | 2 bytes: 'A' and '\0' |

| Type | Size | Range / precision | printf |
|---|---|---|---|
| char | 1 | −128 … 127 (signed) | %c, %d |
| unsigned char | 1 | 0 … 255 | %u |
| short | 2 | −32,768 … 32,767 | %hd |
| int | 4 | −2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647 | %d |
| unsigned int | 4 | 0 … 4,294,967,295 | %u |
| long | 8 (Linux) / 4 (Windows) | | %ld |
| long long | 8 | | %lld |
| float | 4 | ~6–7 digits | %f, %e |
| double | 8 | ~15–16 digits | %lf in scanf, %f in printf |
- Old 16-bit Turbo C: int = 2 bytes (−32,768 … 32,767) – some old questions assume this; read the question.
- Escape sequences: `\n` newline, `\t` tab, `\0` null, `\\` backslash, `\'`, `\"`, `\a` bell, `\b` backspace, `\r` carriage return.

## Output tracing – worked examples
| Statement | Output | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `printf("%d", 'A' + 1);` | 66 | 'A' is 65 |
| `printf("%c", 'a' - 32);` | A | 97 − 32 = 65 |
| `printf("%d", 010 + 0x10);` | 24 | octal 8 + hex 16 |
| `printf("%o %x %X", 65, 255, 255);` | 101 ff FF | octal / hex |
| `printf("%5.2f|", 3.14159);` | ` 3.14\|` | width 5, 2 decimals |
| `printf("%-5d|", 42);` | `42   \|` | `-` = left-justify |
| `printf("%zu", sizeof('A'));` | 4 | a char constant is an int in C (1 in C++) |
| `printf("%zu", sizeof("abc"));` | 4 | 3 chars + '\0' |
| `unsigned char c = 300; printf("%d", c);` | 44 | 300 − 256 |
| `printf("%d", 7 / 2);` | 3 | integer division truncates |
| `printf("%.1f", 7 / 2.0);` | 3.5 | one operand is double |
| `printf("%d %d", 7 % -3, -7 % 3);` | 1 -1 | the remainder takes the sign of the **left** operand |
| `printf("%d", printf("Hi"));` | Hi2 | printf returns the number of characters printed |

## Traps
- A program can have only **one** `main()`; execution always starts there, whatever the order of functions.
- `void main()` is non-standard; `int main(void)` is correct.
- `%f` for an int (or `%d` for a float) prints garbage – undefined behaviour.
- Comments do not nest: `/* a /* b */ c */` ends at the first `*/`.
- C is case-sensitive: `Printf` is an unknown function.

- **Means:** how C came about.
- **Key facts:** ALGOL 60 → CPL → BCPL (Martin Richards, 1967) → B (Ken Thompson, 1970) → **C by Dennis Ritchie at AT&T Bell Labs, 1972**, to rewrite UNIX. K&R book 1978; ANSI C 1989 (C89/C90); C99, C11, C17, C23.
- **Example:** UNIX, Linux kernel, Windows kernel parts, embedded firmware are written in C.
- **Exam point:** C is called a **middle-level** language (high-level syntax + low-level access via pointers and bit operations).

### Structure of a C programme
- **Means:** the sections a C program is arranged in.
- **Key facts:** documentation (comments) → link (`#include`) → definition (`#define`) → global declarations → `main()` → user-defined functions. Every statement ends with `;`; blocks use `{ }`.
- **Example:** `#include <stdio.h>` · `int main(void) { printf("Hi"); return 0; }`
- **Exam point:** execution always starts at **main()**; only one main per program.

### The C character set
- **Means:** characters allowed in C source code.
- **Key facts:** letters A–Z, a–z; digits 0–9; special symbols `~ ! # % ^ & * ( ) - + = | \ { } [ ] : ; " ' < > , . ? /`; white space (blank, tab, newline). Characters form **tokens**: keywords, identifiers, constants, strings, operators, special symbols.
- **Example:** `sum = a + 5;` has tokens `sum`, `=`, `a`, `+`, `5`, `;` → 6 tokens.
- **Exam point:** count tokens: `printf("%d", x);` → `printf`, `(`, `"%d"`, `,`, `x`, `)`, `;` = **7**.

### Constants
- **Means:** fixed values that do not change while the program runs.
- **Key facts:** literal constants (`25`, `3.14`, `'A'`, `"KEA"`), symbolic constants (`#define PI 3.14`), `const` variables (`const int MAX = 100;`).
- **Example:** `const int n = 5; n = 6;` → compile error (assignment of read-only variable).
- **Exam point:** `#define` has no type and no memory; `const` has a type.

### Variables
- **Means:** named memory locations whose value can change.
- **Key facts:** must be **declared** before use with a type; declaration reserves memory; initialise to avoid garbage; naming rules = identifier rules.
- **Example:** `int age = 30; age = age + 1;` → 31.
- **Exam point:** an uninitialised local (auto) variable holds **garbage**; global/static start at 0.

### Keywords
- **Means:** reserved words with a fixed meaning; cannot be used as names.
- **Key facts:** **32 keywords in C89**: auto, break, case, char, const, continue, default, do, double, else, enum, extern, float, for, goto, if, int, long, register, return, short, signed, sizeof, static, struct, switch, typedef, union, unsigned, void, volatile, while. All lowercase.
- **Example:** `int int = 5;` → error. `int Int = 5;` → valid (C is case-sensitive).
- **Exam point:** `main`, `printf`, `include`, `define` are **not** keywords.

### Types of constants
- **Means:** classes of constant values.
- **Key facts:** **Primary** – integer (decimal `25`, octal `031`, hex `0x19`), real/floating (`3.5`, exponent form `2.5e-3`), character (`'a'`, escape `'\n'`). **Secondary** – string, array, pointer, structure, union, enum.
- **Example:** `printf("%d", 031);` → 25.
- **Exam point:** `'A'` (char, 1 character) ≠ `"A"` (string, 2 bytes with `'\0'`); a leading 0 makes an integer **octal** (`08` is an error).

### Types of variables
- **Means:** classified by data type (and by scope/storage).
- **Key facts:** by type: `char` (1 byte), `int` (4), `float` (4), `double` (8), with modifiers `short`, `long`, `signed`, `unsigned`; by scope: **local** (inside a block) and **global** (outside all functions); by storage: auto, register, static, extern.
- **Example:** `unsigned int u = -1;` → stored as 4294967295.
- **Exam point:** `%d` int, `%f` float, `%lf` double (scanf), `%c` char, `%u` unsigned, `%ld` long.

notes.md:
## Instructions (Kanetkar)
- Type declaration, arithmetic, control instructions
- Arithmetic: variable on the left (`a + b = c` is invalid); `%` only for integers; no power operator – `pow()`
- int / int → int (5 / 2 = 2); one real operand → real (5.0 / 2 = 2.5); `float a = 5 / 2` → 2.0
- Assignment converts: `int k = 7.9 / 2` → 3; `char ch = 321` → 65
- Casts: `(float) a / b` = 3.5 but `(float)(a / b)` = 3.0 (a = 7, b = 2)
- C99: −7 / 2 = −3, −7 % 2 = −1 (sign of the dividend)

## Hierarchy of operators (high → low)
| Level | Operators | Assoc. |
|---|---|---|
| Postfix | `() [] -> .` `x++` | L→R |
| Unary | `! ~ ++ -- + - * & sizeof (type)` | R→L |
| Multiplicative | `* / %` | L→R |
| Additive | `+ -` | L→R |
| Shift | `<< >>` | L→R |
| Relational | `< <= > >=` | L→R |
| Equality | `== !=` | L→R |
| Bitwise | `&` then `^` then `|` | L→R |
| Logical | `&&` then `||` | L→R |
| Conditional | `?:` | R→L |
| Assignment | `= += -= …` | R→L |
| Comma | `,` | L→R |
- `&&` / `||` short-circuit; `5 > 3 > 1` = 0; `a & b == c` = `a & (b == c)`; `x = (1, 2, 3)` = 3
- Worked: `2*3/4 + 4/4 + 8 - 2 + 5/8` = 8; `10 + 20*3/4%5` = 10

## Input-output
- Formatted: `printf`, `scanf` (needs `&var`; returns the count read; `%s` stops at white space)
- Unformatted: `getchar putchar gets puts` (`getch getche` in conio.h)
- printf returns the number of characters printed (`printf("happy")` → 5); `%5.2f`, `%-5d`, `%%`

notes.md:
## Three kinds of instructions
1. **Type declaration** – `int a = 5, b = a * 2;` (a variable must be declared before use; `int b = a, a = 5;` is an error)
2. **Arithmetic** – `left = expression;` the left side must be a variable (`a + b = c;` is an error – "lvalue required")
3. **Control** – sequence, decision (if, switch), repetition (loops), case control (goto)

## Operator precedence (high → low) and associativity
| Level | Operators | Assoc. |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `()` `[]` `->` `.` postfix `++ --` | L → R |
| 2 | unary `! ~ + -` prefix `++ --` `*` `&` `(type)` `sizeof` | **R → L** |
| 3 | `* / %` | L → R |
| 4 | `+ -` | L → R |
| 5 | `<< >>` | L → R |
| 6 | `< <= > >=` | L → R |
| 7 | `== !=` | L → R |
| 8–10 | `&` then `^` then `\|` | L → R |
| 11–12 | `&&` then `\|\|` | L → R |
| 13 | `?:` | **R → L** |
| 14 | `= += -= *= /= %= &= ^= \|= <<= >>=` | **R → L** |
| 15 | `,` | L → R |
Memory aid: **unary > arithmetic > shift > relational > equality > bitwise > logical > ternary > assignment > comma**.

## Evaluating expressions – worked examples
- `int a = 2 + 3 * 4 % 5 - 6 / 4;` → 3 * 4 = 12, 12 % 5 = 2, 6 / 4 = 1 → 2 + 2 − 1 = **3**
- `int k = 5 / 2 * 2.0;` → 5 / 2 = 2 (int), 2 × 2.0 = 4.0 → k = **4**
- `float f = 5 / 2;` → **2.000000** (the division happens in int first)
- `float g = (float)5 / 2;` → **2.500000** (cast binds tighter than /)
- `int x = 10 > 5 > 2;` → (10 > 5) = 1, then 1 > 2 = **0**
- `printf("%d", -1 < 1u);` → **0**: −1 is converted to unsigned (4,294,967,295)
- `int a = 5; a += a *= 2;` – modifies a twice without a sequence point → **undefined**
- `int x = (1, 2, 3);` → **3** (comma operator gives the last value). But `x = 1, 2;` sets x to **1** (= binds tighter than ,)
- `int m = a > b ? a : b;` → the larger; nested `a > b ? (a > c ? a : c) : (b > c ? b : c)` → largest of three
- `printf("%d", 5 == 5.0);` → 1 (5 is converted to double)

## Increment / decrement
| Code (i starts at 5 each time) | Result |
|---|---|
| `j = i++;` | j = 5, i = 6 (use, then increment) |
| `j = ++i;` | j = 6, i = 6 (increment, then use) |
| `j = i++ + 10;` | j = 15, i = 6 |
| `j = --i * 2;` | j = 8, i = 4 |
| `j = i++ + ++i;` | **undefined** (i changed twice) – answer "compiler dependent" |
| `printf("%d %d", i, i++);` | **undefined** (order of argument evaluation is unspecified) |

## Short-circuit evaluation (tracing favourite)
```c
int i = 0, j = 5, k;
k = i && ++j;     /* i is 0 → right side skipped: k = 0, j = 5 */
k = i || ++j;     /* right side runs: j = 6, k = 1 */
k = ++i || j++;   /* i = 1 is true → j++ skipped: k = 1, j = 6 */
```

## Type conversion
- Implicit (promotion): char, short → int → unsigned → long → long long → float → double → long double
- In assignment the value is converted to the **left** type: `int n = 3.99;` → 3; `char c = 65.7;` → 'A'
- Explicit cast: `(double)a / b`

## I/O instructions
- `printf` returns characters printed; `scanf` returns **number of items read** (EOF at end of input)
- `scanf("%d", &n);` needs `&`; strings don't: `scanf("%s", name);` (stops at a space – use `fgets` for a line)
- `scanf("%d %d", &a, &b)` – a space in the format skips any white space
- `getchar()` / `putchar()` one character; `puts(s)` prints and **adds a newline**; `gets` was removed in C11 (buffer overflow)
- `sizeof` does not evaluate its operand: `int i = 5; sizeof(i++);` → i is still **5**

## Traps
- `if (x = 0)` assigns 0 → condition is always false; `if (x == 0)` compares
- `a = b = c = 10;` works (right-to-left)
- `%` works only on integers (`5.5 % 2` is an error; use `fmod`)
- `x & 1 == 0` parses as `x & (1 == 0)` → always 0 (see Bitwise notes)

notes.title: KRIES syllabus word by word – C instructions
notes.md:
> **Syllabus:** Type declaration and arithmetic instructions, integer and float conversions, type conversion in assignment, operators in C, hierarchy of operators, control instructions, formatted and unformatted input-output statements

### Type declaration instruction
- **Means:** the statement that declares variables and their types.
- **Key facts:** written at the start of a block (C89); can initialise; can use earlier variables: `int a = 5, b = a * 2;`
- **Example:** `float r = 2.5, area;`
- **Exam point:** `int b = a, a = 5;` is wrong – a is used before it is declared.

### Arithmetic instruction
- **Means:** `variable = expression;` using arithmetic operators.
- **Key facts:** left side must be a single variable (lvalue); operators `+ - * / %`; `%` only for integers; no implicit multiplication (`a = bc` is not b × c).
- **Example:** `k = 3 * 4 + 6 / 4;` → 12 + 1 = **13**.
- **Exam point:** `a + b = c;` → error "lvalue required"; `x = 5 % 2.0` → error.

### Integer and float conversions
- **Means:** what type the result of an arithmetic operation has.
- **Key facts:** int op int → **int**; float op float → float; int op float → **float** (the int is promoted).
- **Example:** `5 / 2` = 2 · `5.0 / 2` = 2.5 · `5 / 2.0` = 2.5 · `2 / 5` = 0 · `2.0 / 5` = 0.4.
- **Exam point:** integer division **truncates** toward zero: `-7 / 2` = −3.

### Type conversion in assignment
- **Means:** when the right-side type differs from the left variable's type, the value is converted to the **left** type.
- **Key facts:** float → int drops the fraction; int → float adds `.0`; large int → char keeps the low byte.
- **Example:** `int i = 3.99;` → 3 · `float f = 7 / 2;` → 3.000000 · `char c = 321;` → 65 ('A').
- **Exam point:** in `float a = 9 / 2 * 2;` the right side is done in int: 4 × 2 = 8 → a = 8.0.

### Operators in C
- **Means:** symbols that perform operations.
- **Key facts:** arithmetic `+ - * / %`; relational `< > <= >= == !=`; logical `&& || !`; bitwise `& | ^ ~ << >>`; assignment `= += -= …`; increment/decrement `++ --`; conditional `?:`; comma `,`; `sizeof`; address `&`, indirection `*`; member `.` and `->`.
- **Example:** `x = 10; y = x++ * 2;` → y = 20, x = 11.
- **Exam point:** `?:` is the only **ternary** operator; `sizeof` is an operator, not a function.

### Hierarchy of operators
- **Means:** order (precedence) and direction (associativity) of evaluation.
- **Key facts:** `()` → unary (`! ~ ++ -- - sizeof (type)`, right-to-left) → `* / %` → `+ -` → `<< >>` → `< <= > >=` → `== !=` → `&` → `^` → `|` → `&&` → `||` → `?:` → assignment (right-to-left) → `,`.
- **Example:** `i = 2 * 3 / 4 + 4 / 4 + 8 - 2 + 5 / 8;` → 1 + 1 + 8 − 2 + 0 = **8** (2 × 3 = 6, 6 / 4 = 1).
- **Exam point:** `*` and `/` have equal precedence → evaluate **left to right**; `a = b = c` goes right to left.

### Control instructions
- **Means:** instructions that decide the order in which statements run.
- **Key facts:** four kinds – **sequence** (one after another), **selection/decision** (if, if-else, switch), **repetition/loop** (while, do-while, for), **case control** (switch; goto).
- **Example:** `if (marks >= 35) puts("Pass"); else puts("Fail");`
- **Exam point:** without control instructions, statements run in sequence.

### Formatted input-output statements
- **Means:** I/O functions that use format specifiers.
- **Key facts:** `printf()` and `scanf()` (`<stdio.h>`); specifiers `%d %i %u %ld %f %lf %e %c %s %x %o %p %%`; width/precision `%6.2f`, left-align `%-5d`, leading zeros `%05d`.
- **Example:** `printf("%05d|%-4d|%.3f", 42, 7, 3.14159);` → `00042|7   |3.142`
- **Exam point:** `scanf` needs addresses (`&x`); it returns the number of values read; `printf` returns the number of characters printed.

### Unformatted input-output statements
- **Means:** I/O without format specifiers – character and string functions.
- **Key facts:** `getchar()` / `putchar()` (one char, stdio.h); `getch()` / `getche()` (conio.h, no Enter needed – non-standard); `gets()` / `puts()` (strings; puts adds a newline; gets removed in C11 → use `fgets`).
- **Example:** `char c = getchar(); putchar(c + 1);` → typing `a` prints `b`.
- **Exam point:** `getch()` does not echo; `getche()` echoes; `scanf("%s")` stops at a space, `gets/fgets` read the whole line.

notes.title: Control structures – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Decisions
- `if`, `if-else`, nested if, `else if` ladder; non-zero = true, 0 = false; relational results are 1/0 (int)
- Traps: `if (x = 5)` is always true; `if (a > b);` has an empty body; without braces only one statement belongs to the if
- **Dangling else** pairs with the nearest unmatched `if`
- `10 <= x <= 20` is always true – write `x >= 10 && x <= 20`
- `&&`, `||` short-circuit (right side may not run: `i++ || j++`)
- `?:` – three operands, right-associative; `max = a > b ? a : b`
- Never compare floats with `==` (`0.1f != 0.1`)
- Leap year: `(y % 4 == 0 && y % 100 != 0) || y % 400 == 0`

## Loops
| Loop | Test | Runs at least |
|---|---|---|
| while | before body | 0 times |
| for (init; test; update) | before body | 0 times (init once) |
| do … while( ); | after body | 1 time |
- `for (;;)` and `while (1)` are infinite; `for (i = 0; i < 5; i++);` – the `;` is the body (i ends at 5)
- `break` – leaves the innermost loop/switch; `continue` – next iteration; `goto label;` – jump within a function; `exit()` – ends the program
- Counting: `for (i = 1; i <= 100; i *= 2)` runs 7 times; `while (i++ < 5)` tests 6 times and leaves i = 6

## switch
- Expression and case labels must be integer types (int, char, enum) – no float, no ranges, no duplicates
- Without `break` control falls through to the next case; `default` may be anywhere

```c
if (a > 10)
    if (b > 5) printf("X");
else printf("Y");      /* belongs to if (b > 5) → nothing printed */
```

## switch
- Case labels must be **integer or character constants** (no float, no string, no variables, no ranges in standard C)
- Without `break` execution **falls through** to the next cases; `default` can be anywhere and is optional
```c
int x = 2;
switch (x) {
    case 1: printf("A");
    case 2: printf("B");
    case 3: printf("C"); break;
    default: printf("D");
}                                   /* output: BC */
```
- `switch (x) { default: printf("D"); case 1: printf("A"); }` with x = 5 → **DA** (default falls through too)
- Duplicate case values are a compile error; `case 'a': case 'A':` share one block

## Loops
| Loop | Test | Runs at least once? |
|---|---|---|
| `while (cond)` | entry-controlled | no |
| `for (init; cond; update)` | entry-controlled | no |
| `do { } while (cond);` | **exit-controlled** | **yes** (note the `;` at the end) |

## Tracing loops – worked examples
| Code | Output / result |
|---|---|
| `for (i = 0; i < 5; i++); printf("%d", i);` | **5** – the `;` is an empty body |
| `i = 0; while (i < 10) i += 3; printf("%d", i);` | **12** |
| `for (i = 1; i <= 10; i *= 2) n++;` | i = 1, 2, 4, 8 → n = **4** |
| `for (i = 10; i > 0; i -= 3) printf("%d ", i);` | 10 7 4 1 |
| `i = 0; do printf("%d", i); while (i++ < 3);` | **0123** |
| `i = 5; while (i--) printf("%d", i);` | **43210** (test uses 5…1, prints after decrement) |
| `for (i = 0, j = 10; i < j; i++, j--) n++;` | n = **5** |
| `for (i = 1; i <= 3; i++) for (j = 1; j <= i; j++) n++;` | 1 + 2 + 3 = **6** |

Counting rule: a loop `for (i = a; i <= b; i += s)` runs ⌊(b − a)/s⌋ + 1 times when a ≤ b.

## break, continue, goto
- `break` leaves the **innermost** loop or switch only
- `continue` skips to the next iteration (in a `for`, the update part still runs)
```c
for (i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
    if (i == 3) continue;
    if (i == 5) break;
    printf("%d ", i);
}                                   /* 1 2 4 */
```
- `goto label;` jumps anywhere in the same function (avoid; used to leave deep nesting)

## Classic loop programs (know the logic)
- **Sum of digits** of 1234: `while (n) { s += n % 10; n /= 10; }` → 10
- **Reverse** 1234: `r = r * 10 + n % 10;` → 4321; palindrome if reverse == original
- **Armstrong** (3 digits): 153 = 1³ + 5³ + 3³; 370, 371, 407 are the others
- **Prime**: test divisors 2 … √n; **factorial** 5! = 120; **Fibonacci** 0 1 1 2 3 5 8 13
- **GCD** (Euclid): `while (b) { t = b; b = a % b; a = t; }` → gcd(48, 18) = 6; lcm = a × b / gcd = 144
- Patterns: outer loop = rows, inner loop = columns (`for (j = 1; j <= i; j++) printf("*");`)

## Traps
- `for (unsigned i = 5; i >= 0; i--)` never ends (unsigned is never negative)
- `while (x != 10) x += 3;` with x = 0 never ends (0, 3, 6, 9, 12 … skips 10)
- `if (a = 5)` is always true; `while (0)` body never runs; `for (;;)` is an infinite loop
- A `case` without `break` is not an error – it is fall-through

notes.title: KRIES syllabus word by word – Control structures
notes.md:
> **Syllabus:** Decision control structures, logical, conditional and relational operators; loops – while, do-while, for; break, continue, switch-case, goto

### Decision control structures
- **Means:** statements that choose which code runs.
- **Key facts:** `if`, `if-else`, nested if, `else-if` ladder, `switch`; condition is true when **non-zero**.
- **Example:** `if (n % 2 == 0) puts("even"); else puts("odd");`
- **Exam point:** an `else` pairs with the **nearest** unmatched `if`; `if (x = 5)` is always true.

### Logical operators
- **Means:** combine conditions: `&&` (AND), `||` (OR), `!` (NOT); result is 1 or 0.
- **Key facts:** **short-circuit**: in `a && b`, b is skipped if a is 0; in `a || b`, b is skipped if a is non-zero. `!` has the highest precedence of the three, then `&&`, then `||`.
- **Example:** `int i = 0, j = 2; if (i && j++) ; printf("%d", j);` → 2.
- **Exam point:** `!5` = 0, `!0` = 1; `5 && 3` = 1.

### Conditional operator
- **Means:** `condition ? value1 : value2` – a compact if-else that gives a value.
- **Key facts:** the only ternary operator; right-to-left associative; can be nested.
- **Example:** `big = (a > b) ? a : b;` · `printf("%s", n % 2 ? "odd" : "even");`
- **Exam point:** `x = 5 > 3 ? 10 : 20;` → 10.

### Relational operators
- **Means:** compare values: `< > <= >= == !=`; result 1 (true) or 0 (false).
- **Key facts:** `==` compares, `=` assigns; relational ops are higher in precedence than `==` and `!=`.
- **Example:** `printf("%d", 3 < 2 < 1);` → (0 < 1) = **1**.
- **Exam point:** compare floats with a tolerance, not `==` (0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3 in binary).

### Loops – while
- **Means:** entry-controlled loop: test first, then body.
- **Key facts:** `while (cond) { … }` – may run zero times; update the variable inside or it never ends.
- **Example:** `i = 1; while (i <= 5) { s += i; i++; }` → s = 15.
- **Exam point:** `while (i < 5);` (semicolon) → empty body → infinite loop if i < 5.

### Loops – do-while
- **Means:** exit-controlled loop: body first, then test.
- **Key facts:** runs **at least once**; syntax ends with `while (cond);`
- **Example:** `i = 10; do { printf("%d", i); } while (i < 5);` → prints 10 once.
- **Exam point:** best for menus that must appear at least once.

### Loops – for
- **Means:** `for (initialisation; condition; update)` – compact counting loop.
- **Key facts:** any part may be empty: `for (;;)` = infinite; comma for several variables: `for (i = 0, j = 9; i < j; i++, j--)`.
- **Example:** `for (i = 1; i <= 10; i += 3) printf("%d ", i);` → 1 4 7 10.
- **Exam point:** the update runs **after** the body, before the next test; after the loop i holds the first failing value.

### break
- **Means:** leave the nearest enclosing loop or switch immediately.
- **Key facts:** only one level; in nested loops the outer loop continues.
- **Example:** `for (i = 1; i <= 10; i++) { if (i == 4) break; printf("%d", i); }` → 123.
- **Exam point:** `break` outside a loop/switch → compile error.

### continue
- **Means:** skip the rest of the current iteration and go to the next one.
- **Key facts:** in a `for`, control goes to the **update** part; in while/do-while, to the test.
- **Example:** `for (i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { if (i % 2 == 0) continue; printf("%d", i); }` → 135.
- **Exam point:** `continue` cannot be used in a switch on its own (only inside a loop).

### switch-case
- **Means:** multi-way selection on an integer/char value.
- **Key facts:** `case` labels must be **constant integer/char** expressions, unique; `default` optional and can be anywhere; no `break` → **fall-through**.
- **Example:** `switch (2) { case 1: printf("A"); case 2: printf("B"); case 3: printf("C"); }` → BC.
- **Exam point:** `switch` cannot test float, string or ranges (`case 1 ... 5` is a GCC extension only).

### goto
- **Means:** unconditional jump to a **label** in the same function.
- **Key facts:** `goto end; … end: statement;` – makes code hard to read ("spaghetti code"); acceptable to escape deeply nested loops.
- **Example:** `i = 1; loop: printf("%d", i++); if (i <= 3) goto loop;` → 123.
- **Exam point:** cannot jump into another function; structured programming avoids goto.

notes.title: Arrays and strings – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Arrays
- `int a[5];` indices 0–4; no bounds checking (a[5] or a[-1] → garbage / undefined)
- `int a[5] = {1, 2};` → rest 0; `int a[] = {…}` size from initialisers; count = `sizeof(a) / sizeof(a[0])`
- 2-D row-major: address of a[i][j] = base + (i × cols + j) × size; `char a[100][100]` → a[40][50] at 4050
- `int a[3][2] = {1,2,3,4,5,6}` → a[2][1] = 6; `int a[2][3][4]` = 24 elements
- Array name = `&a[0]` (cannot be assigned: `a = b` is an error); `2[a]` = `a[2]`
- Bubble sort: n − 1 passes, n(n − 1)/2 comparisons, O(n²) (O(n) best with a swap flag); largest element moves to the end after each pass
  - [4,3,2,1,8,7,6,5] → pass 1: 3 2 1 4 7 6 5 8 → pass 2: 2 1 3 4 6 5 7 8

## Strings
- char array ending in `'\0'`; `"hi"` takes 3 bytes; `sizeof("bengaluru")` = 10, `strlen` = 9
- `char s[10]; s = "hi";` is an error – use `strcpy(s, "hi")`
- `<string.h>`: strlen, strcpy(dest, src), strncpy, strcat(dest, src), strncmp, strcmp (0 when equal), strchr (char), strstr (substring), strrev (Turbo C)
- `<ctype.h>`: toupper, tolower, isdigit, isalpha; `<stdlib.h>`: atoi, atof
- `scanf("%s")` stops at a space; `gets` removed (use `fgets`); compare contents with strcmp, not ==
- `'a' − 32 = 'A'`; palindrome: s[i] vs s[n − 1 − i]

notes.title: Arrays and strings – detailed notes with worked examples
notes.md:
## Declaring and initialising
- `int a[5] = {1, 2};` → {1, 2, 0, 0, 0} (missing elements become 0); `int a[5];` (local) holds garbage
- `int a[] = {4, 5, 6};` → size 3; number of elements = `sizeof(a) / sizeof(a[0])`
- Index runs 0 … n − 1; **no bounds checking** – `a[5]` on a 5-element array is undefined, not an error
- Size must be a constant in C89 (C99 allows variable-length arrays)
- An array name is a constant address: `a++` and `a = b` are errors; copy element by element (or memcpy)

## Address calculation (formula questions)
- 1-D: **addr(a[i]) = base + (i − LB) × w**
- 2-D, **row-major** (C): **addr(a[i][j]) = base + ((i − LR) × columns + (j − LC)) × w**
- 2-D, column-major (Fortran): base + ((j − LC) × rows + (i − LR)) × w
- Example: `int a[3][4]`, base 1000, w = 4 → a[2][1] = 1000 + (2 × 4 + 1) × 4 = **1036**
- Example: A[−2..5][3..8], base 500, w = 2 → 8 rows, 6 columns → A[1][5] row-major = 500 + ((1 + 2) × 6 + (5 − 3)) × 2 = **540**; column-major = 500 + ((5 − 3) × 8 + (1 + 2)) × 2 = **538**

## 2-D arrays
- `int m[2][3] = {{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}};` – the first dimension may be omitted: `int m[][3] = {...}`; the column size never
- Matrix multiplication A(m × n) · B(n × p) is possible only when columns of A = rows of B → result m × p, needs m·n·p multiplications
- Transpose: `t[j][i] = m[i][j]`; sum of the diagonal: `m[i][i]`

## Strings
- A string is a char array ending in `'\0'`
- `char s[] = "hello";` → sizeof 6, strlen 5; `char s[5] = "hello";` is legal in C but has **no '\0'** (printing it is undefined)
- `char *p = "hello";` points to a read-only literal – `p[0] = 'H'` is undefined; `char s[] = "hello"; s[0] = 'H';` is fine

| `<string.h>` | Does | Example |
|---|---|---|
| strlen(s) | length without '\0' | strlen("abc\0de") = **3** |
| strcpy(d, s) | copy s into d | d must be big enough |
| strncpy(d, s, n) | copy at most n | may leave no '\0' |
| strcat(d, s) | append | "Exam" + "Sim" → "ExamSim" |
| strcmp(a, b) | < 0, 0, > 0 | strcmp("abc", "abd") < 0; strcmp("b", "a") > 0 |
| strchr(s, c) / strstr(s, t) | first char / substring | return a pointer or NULL |
| strrev, strupr, strlwr | non-standard (Turbo C) | |
- Comparing with `==` compares **addresses**, not contents – use strcmp

## Output tracing
```c
char s[] = "ExamSim";
printf("%c", s[3]);        /* m      */
printf("%s", s + 4);       /* Sim    */
printf("%c", *s + 1);      /* F  ('E' + 1) */
printf("%c", *(s + 1));    /* x      */
printf("%zu %zu", sizeof(s), strlen(s));   /* 8 7 */
int a[] = {10, 20, 30, 40};
printf("%d", a[1] + a[3]);   /* 60 */
printf("%d", 2[a]);          /* 30 – a[i] == *(a+i) == i[a] */
```

## Arrays and functions
- An array is passed as a **pointer** to its first element: changes inside the function affect the caller
- Inside the function `sizeof(arr)` gives the pointer size (8), so pass the length separately
- `void f(int a[])`, `void f(int *a)` and `void f(int a[10])` are identical; 2-D: `void g(int m[][4])`

## Sorting and searching on arrays
- **Bubble sort** on 5 1 4 2 8 – pass 1: 1 4 2 5 8 (the largest bubbles to the end); n − 1 passes, n(n − 1)/2 comparisons
- **Linear search** O(n); **binary search** O(log n) – only on a sorted array (see Searching and Sorting notes)

## Traps
- `int a[3] = {1, 2, 3, 4};` → compile error/warning (too many initialisers)
- Array index can be an expression: `a[i++]`
- `char c[] = {'a', 'b'};` is not a string (no '\0')

notes.title: KRIES syllabus word by word – Arrays
notes.md:
> **Syllabus:** One- and multi-dimensional arrays – declaration, initialisation, manipulation; bubble sort; strings – basic concepts and library functions

### One-dimensional array
- **Means:** a list of same-type elements in contiguous memory, accessed by one index.
- **Key facts:** index 0 … n−1; address of a[i] = base + i × size; size = n × sizeof(element).
- **Example:** `int a[5]` with base 1000 → a[3] at 1012; total 20 bytes.
- **Exam point:** C does no bounds checking.

### Multi-dimensional array
- **Means:** array of arrays – e.g. a matrix `int m[3][4]` (3 rows, 4 columns).
- **Key facts:** stored **row-major**; a[i][j] at base + (i × columns + j) × size; 3-D: `int c[2][3][4]` = 24 elements.
- **Example:** `int m[3][4]`, base 2000 → m[1][2] = 2000 + (1 × 4 + 2) × 4 = **2024**.
- **Exam point:** total elements = product of dimensions.

### Declaration
- **Means:** telling the compiler the type, name and size.
- **Key facts:** `type name[size];` size must be a positive constant in C89 (VLA allowed in C99); `int a[0]`, `int a[-3]` are errors.
- **Example:** `float marks[60]; char name[30]; int m[2][3];`
- **Exam point:** in a 2-D declaration with initialiser, only the **first** dimension may be omitted.

### Initialisation
- **Means:** giving values at declaration.
- **Key facts:** `int a[5] = {1, 2, 3};` → remaining are 0; `int a[] = {1, 2, 3};` → size 3; `int a[5] = {0};` → all zeros; `int m[2][3] = {{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}};` or `{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}`.
- **Example:** `int a[4] = {5}; printf("%d", a[0] + a[3]);` → 5.
- **Exam point:** more initialisers than the size → error; uninitialised local array → garbage.

### Manipulation
- **Means:** reading, printing, updating, searching, summing, copying arrays with loops.
- **Key facts:** traverse `for (i = 0; i < n; i++)`; copy element by element (`b = a` is illegal); find max: start with a[0].
- **Example:** reverse in place: `for (i = 0; i < n / 2; i++) { t = a[i]; a[i] = a[n-1-i]; a[n-1-i] = t; }`
- **Exam point:** inserting at position k needs shifting elements right from the end.

### Bubble sort
- **Means:** repeatedly swap adjacent elements that are out of order; the largest "bubbles" to the end each pass.
- **Key facts:** n − 1 passes; n(n − 1)/2 comparisons; O(n²) worst/average, O(n) best with a swap flag; stable.
- **Example:** 5 1 4 2 8 → pass 1: 1 4 2 5 8 → pass 2: 1 2 4 5 8 (sorted).
- **Exam point:** after pass k the last k elements are in final position.

### Strings – basic concepts
- **Means:** a character array terminated by the null character `'\0'`.
- **Key facts:** `char s[] = "KEA";` → 4 bytes; `%s` prints till `'\0'`; `scanf("%s", s)` (no &) stops at space; string literal is read-only when used through a pointer.
- **Example:** `char s[10] = "Hi"; printf("%zu %zu", sizeof(s), strlen(s));` → 10 2.
- **Exam point:** `"A"` takes 2 bytes, `'A'` 1 byte.

### Library functions (string.h)
- **Means:** ready functions for strings.
- **Key facts:** `strlen` (length without '\0'), `strcpy(d, s)`, `strncpy`, `strcat(d, s)`, `strcmp(a, b)` (0 if equal, <0 / >0 by first differing character), `strncmp`, `strchr`, `strstr`, `strrev`/`strupr`/`strlwr` (Turbo C only); ctype.h: `toupper`, `isalpha`, `isdigit`.
- **Example:** `char a[20] = "Com"; strcat(a, "puter"); printf("%s %zu", a, strlen(a));` → Computer 8.
- **Exam point:** compare strings with **strcmp**, not `==`.

notes.title: Functions – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Definition and prototypes
- Declaration (prototype) `float avg(int, int);` → definition `float avg(int a, int b) { … }` → call `avg(x, y)`
- Actual arguments (in the call) vs formal parameters (in the definition)
- One return value at most; `void f(void)` = no arguments, no value; C89 default return type int
- Categories: no args/no return, args/no return, no args/return, args/return; library vs user-defined
- C passes **by value**; pass an address (`&x`) to let a function change the caller's variable (call by reference)
- No overloading; no nested function definitions; a file-level `static` function is private to its file

## Recursion
- Needs a base case, else stack overflow; one activation record per active call
- fact(5) → 6 calls; fib(n) is exponential; `fun(2)` with `n == 4 ? n : 2*fun(n+1)` = 16
- Print before the call → 3 2 1; print after the call → 1 2 3
- gcd(a, b) = b == 0 ? a : gcd(b, a % b)

## Passing arrays
- `f(int a[])` = `f(int *a)` – the address is passed; changes affect the caller; `sizeof(a)` inside = pointer size

## Storage classes
| Class | Storage | Default | Scope | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| auto | stack | garbage | block | block |
| register | CPU register | garbage | block | block (no `&`) |
| static | data segment | 0 | block / file | whole run (keeps value) |
| extern | data segment | 0 | global (other files) | whole run |
- `static int x = 3; x++; if (x <= 6) { printf("World"); main(); }` → World ×3

notes.title: Functions – detailed notes with worked examples
notes.md:
## Parts of a function
```c
int add(int, int);              /* declaration / prototype */
int main(void) {
    printf("%d", add(2, 3));    /* call: 2, 3 are actual arguments */
    return 0;
}
int add(int x, int y) {         /* definition: x, y are formal parameters */
    return x + y;               /* returns ONE value */
}
```
- A function can return only one value (return a struct or use pointers for more)
- Types of functions: library (printf, sqrt) vs user-defined; by arguments/return value – no args no return, args no return, no args return, args and return

## Call by value vs call by reference
| By value | By reference (address) |
|---|---|
| a **copy** is passed | the **address** is passed (`&x`) |
| changes stay inside the function | changes reach the caller |
| `void swap(int a, int b)` – does **not** swap | `void swap(int *a, int *b)` – swaps |
```c
void swap(int *a, int *b) { int t = *a; *a = *b; *b = t; }
int x = 1, y = 2; swap(&x, &y);      /* x = 2, y = 1 */
```
C itself passes everything by value; "call by reference" means passing an address by value.

## Storage classes
| Class | Stored in | Default | Scope | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| auto (default for locals) | stack | garbage | block | block |
| register | CPU register (request) | garbage | block | block – `&` not allowed |
| **static** (local) | data segment | **0** | block | **whole program – keeps its value** |
| static (global) | data segment | 0 | **this file only** | whole program |
| extern | data segment | 0 | all files | whole program – declares, doesn't allocate |
```c
void count(void) { static int c = 0; c++; printf("%d ", c); }
count(); count(); count();          /* 1 2 3  (with auto: 1 1 1) */
```
- A static local is initialised **once**, and only with a constant.

## Recursion – trace the calls
- Needs a **base case**; each call gets its own stack frame; too deep → stack overflow
```c
int fact(int n) { return n <= 1 ? 1 : n * fact(n - 1); }   /* fact(5) = 120 */
int sum(int n)  { return n == 0 ? 0 : n % 10 + sum(n / 10); } /* sum(1234) = 10 */
int pw(int b, int e) { return e == 0 ? 1 : b * pw(b, e - 1); } /* pw(2, 5) = 32 */
void up(int n)   { if (n > 0) { up(n - 1); printf("%d ", n); } }   /* up(3): 1 2 3 */
void down(int n) { if (n > 0) { printf("%d ", n); down(n - 1); } } /* down(3): 3 2 1 */
```
- Statement **after** the recursive call runs on the way back (reverse order)
- `fib(n) = fib(n−1) + fib(n−2)`: fib(5) = 5 (0 1 1 2 3 5); the naive version makes **15 calls** for fib(5) → O(2ⁿ)
- `int f(int n) { if (n <= 0) return 0; return n + f(n - 2); }` → f(7) = 7 + 5 + 3 + 1 = **16**
- Tower of Hanoi: 2ⁿ − 1 moves; Ackermann grows extremely fast (not primitive recursive)

## main and command-line arguments
- `int main(int argc, char *argv[])`: `./prog in.txt 5` → argc = 3, argv[0] = "./prog", argv[1] = "in.txt", argv[2] = "5" (a string – use atoi)
- `return 0` = success; `exit(1)` ends the program from anywhere (`<stdlib.h>`)

## Library functions to remember
- `<math.h>`: sqrt, pow, fabs, ceil(2.1) = 3.0, floor(2.9) = 2.0, round, log, exp, sin – link with `-lm`
- `<stdlib.h>`: abs, atoi("42") = 42, rand, srand, malloc, free, exit, qsort
- `<ctype.h>`: isdigit, isalpha, isupper, toupper('a') = 'A'

## Traps
- Calling a function before its prototype assumes it returns int (old C) – in C99 it is an error
- A function's arguments are evaluated in **unspecified order**
- Returning the address of a local variable → dangling pointer
- `return` with no value in an int function returns garbage
- Nested function **definitions** are not allowed in standard C (calls inside calls are fine)

notes.title: KRIES syllabus word by word – Functions
notes.md:
> **Syllabus:** Definition, function definition and prototyping, types of functions and arguments, recursion, passing arrays to functions; storage classes – automatic, register, external, static

### Definition (of a function)
- **Means:** a self-contained block of statements that performs a task and may return a value.
- **Key facts:** benefits – reuse, modularity, easier testing; `main()` is itself a function; library vs user-defined.
- **Example:** `int sq(int x) { return x * x; }`
- **Exam point:** a function returns at most **one** value with `return`.

### Function definition
- **Means:** the actual body: `return_type name(parameter list) { body }`.
- **Key facts:** parameters in the definition are **formal**; values in the call are **actual** arguments; `void` return = nothing returned.
- **Example:** `float avg(int a, int b) { return (a + b) / 2.0; }` → avg(3, 4) = 3.5.
- **Exam point:** definitions cannot be nested inside other functions.

### Prototyping
- **Means:** declaring a function before use: `return_type name(parameter types);`
- **Key facts:** lets the compiler check argument number and types; parameter names optional: `int add(int, int);`; usually in header files.
- **Example:** prototype at top, `main()` calls `add(2, 3)`, definition below main.
- **Exam point:** missing prototype → implicit int (C89) or error (C99).

### Types of functions
- **Means:** grouped by arguments and return value.
- **Key facts:** (1) no arguments, no return; (2) arguments, no return; (3) no arguments, return; (4) arguments and return. Also library (printf, sqrt) vs user-defined; recursive.
- **Example:** `void line(void)` (type 1); `int getNum(void)` (type 3).
- **Exam point:** a `void` function used in an expression → error.

### Arguments
- **Means:** values passed to a function.
- **Key facts:** **call by value** – a copy is passed (changes don't affect the caller); **call by reference** – the address is passed (pointer), changes affect the caller; order of argument evaluation is unspecified.
- **Example:** `void inc(int *p) { (*p)++; }` → `inc(&x);` increases x.
- **Exam point:** C itself is call by value; reference is simulated with pointers.

### Recursion
- **Means:** a function calling itself (directly or indirectly).
- **Key facts:** needs a **base case**; uses the stack (one frame per call); can overflow; examples – factorial, Fibonacci, GCD, Tower of Hanoi, binary search.
- **Example:** `int f(int n) { return n == 0 ? 0 : n + f(n - 1); }` → f(4) = 10.
- **Exam point:** statements after the recursive call run in **reverse** order of calls.

### Passing arrays to functions
- **Means:** sending an array to a function – the **address of the first element** is passed.
- **Key facts:** changes inside affect the original; pass the size separately; `void f(int a[], int n)` = `void f(int *a, int n)`; 2-D: column size required `void g(int m[][4], int r)`.
- **Example:** `void zero(int a[], int n) { for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) a[i] = 0; }`
- **Exam point:** `sizeof(a)` inside the function = pointer size (8), not the array size.

### Storage classes – automatic
- **Means:** `auto` – default for local variables.
- **Key facts:** stored on the **stack**; default value **garbage**; scope – the block; lifetime – until the block ends.
- **Example:** `void f() { auto int x = 0; x++; printf("%d", x); }` → prints 1 every call.
- **Exam point:** writing `auto` is optional.

### Storage classes – register
- **Means:** request to keep the variable in a **CPU register** for speed.
- **Key facts:** default garbage; block scope and lifetime; the compiler may ignore it; **`&` not allowed**; used for loop counters.
- **Example:** `register int i; for (i = 0; i < 1000; i++) …`
- **Exam point:** `&i` on a register variable → compile error.

### Storage classes – external
- **Means:** `extern` – a global variable defined elsewhere (another file or later in the same file).
- **Key facts:** stored in the data segment; default **0**; scope – whole program; lifetime – whole run; `extern int x;` declares, does not allocate.
- **Example:** file1.c `int count = 5;` · file2.c `extern int count;`
- **Exam point:** global variables are extern by default.

### Storage classes – static
- **Means:** variable that keeps its value between calls (local static) or is private to the file (global static).
- **Key facts:** data segment; default **0**; initialised **once**; lifetime – whole program.
- **Example:** `void f() { static int c; c++; printf("%d ", c); }` called 3 times → 1 2 3.
- **Exam point:** static local = block scope but program lifetime.

notes.title: Pointers – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Basics
- `int *p = &x;` → `*p` is x; `&` address-of, `*` indirection; `%p` prints addresses
- NULL pointer (points nowhere), wild pointer (uninitialised), dangling pointer (memory freed), void pointer (generic – cast before `*`)
- Pointer size does not depend on the type (8 bytes on 64-bit)
- Arithmetic scales by the type size: int* + 1 → +4; double* + 3 → +24; difference of two pointers = number of elements
- Not allowed: adding, multiplying or dividing pointers
- `const int *p` – value read-only; `int * const q` – pointer fixed
- `<stdlib.h>`: malloc(bytes) (garbage), calloc(n, size) (zeroed), realloc, free; memory leak = never freed

## Pointers and arrays
- `a[i]` = `*(a + i)` = `i[a]`; `a[i][j]` = `*(*(a + i) + j)`; array name is a constant pointer (`a++` illegal)
- `*p++` – use then move; `(*p)++` – increment the value; `++*p` – increment the value first
- `int *a[10]` – array of 10 pointers; `int (*b)[10]` – pointer to an array of 10 ints; `int (*fp)(int, int)` – function pointer
- `char *names[] = {"Ram", "Sita"}` – array of pointers to strings; `argv` is `char *argv[]`
- String literals are read-only (`char *p = "hello"; p[0] = 'H';` is undefined)

## Call by reference and pointers to pointers
- `void swap(int *x, int *y)`; call `swap(&a, &b)`
- `int **q = &p;` → `**q` is the int; `**q + *p` = 2x
- Never return the address of a local variable

notes.title: Pointers – detailed notes with worked examples
notes.md:
## Reading declarations (right–left rule)
| Declaration | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `int *p;` | p is a pointer to int |
| `int **q;` | pointer to pointer to int |
| `int *a[5];` | array of 5 pointers to int |
| `int (*b)[5];` | pointer to an array of 5 ints |
| `int *f(void);` | function returning a pointer to int |
| `int (*fp)(int, int);` | pointer to a function taking two ints and returning int |
| `const int *p;` / `int const *p;` | pointer to a constant int (value read-only) |
| `int *const p = &x;` | constant pointer (cannot point elsewhere) |
| `void *v;` | generic pointer – cast before dereferencing; no arithmetic in standard C |

## Pointer arithmetic (addresses)
p holds 1000:
| Type of p | p + 1 | p + 3 |
|---|---|---|
| char * | 1001 | 1003 |
| int * | 1004 | 1012 |
| double * | 1008 | 1024 |
- Subtracting two pointers into the same array gives the **number of elements** between them: `&a[3] − &a[0]` = 3
- Allowed: pointer ± integer, pointer − pointer, comparison. Not allowed: pointer + pointer, × , ÷
- `sizeof(p)` = 8 for every pointer type on a 64-bit system

## Trace – pointers and arrays
```c
int a[] = {10, 20, 30, 40};
int *p = a;
printf("%d ", *(p + 2));   /* 30                       */
p++;                        /* p → a[1]                 */
printf("%d ", *p);          /* 20                       */
printf("%d ", *p++);        /* 20, then p → a[2]        */
printf("%d ", ++*p);        /* a[2] becomes 31 → 31     */
printf("%d ", (*p)++);      /* prints 31, a[2] = 32     */
printf("%d", *p);           /* 32                       */
```
Output: `30 20 20 31 31 32`
- `*p++` = `*(p++)` (postfix binds tighter) – use the value, move the pointer
- `++*p` and `(*p)++` change the **value**; `*++p` moves first, then reads

## 2-D arrays and pointers
`int m[2][3] = {{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}};`
- `m[i][j]` = `*(*(m + i) + j)`; `**m` = 1; `*m[1]` = 4; `*(*(m + 1) + 2)` = 6
- `m + 1` moves a whole row (12 bytes); `*m + 1` moves one int (4 bytes)

## Strings and pointers
```c
char *s = "hello";
printf("%c", *(s + 1));   /* e     */
printf("%s", s + 2);      /* llo   */
printf("%c", *s + 2);     /* j  ('h' + 2) */
```
- `sizeof(s)` = 8 (pointer) but `char t[] = "hello"; sizeof(t)` = 6
- String length with pointers: `char *q = s; while (*q) q++; len = q − s;`

## Pointer to pointer
```c
int x = 10, *p = &x, **q = &p;
**q = 20;                       /* x is now 20 */
printf("%d %d %d", x, *p, **q); /* 20 20 20    */
```

## Dynamic memory (`<stdlib.h>`)
| Function | Does | Memory content |
|---|---|---|
| `malloc(n)` | n bytes | garbage |
| `calloc(k, size)` | k × size bytes | **zeroed** |
| `realloc(p, n)` | resize (may move) | old data kept |
| `free(p)` | release | p becomes dangling – set `p = NULL` |
```c
int *arr = malloc(5 * sizeof(int));
if (arr == NULL) { /* out of memory */ }
for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) arr[i] = i * i;   /* 0 1 4 9 16 */
free(arr); arr = NULL;
```
- Heap memory lives until free(); forgetting free → **memory leak**; using after free → **dangling pointer**; freeing twice → undefined

## Function pointers
```c
int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
int (*fp)(int, int) = add;     /* or &add */
printf("%d", fp(2, 3));        /* 5 */
```
Used for callbacks (qsort's compare function), menus, tables of operations.

## Traps
- Uninitialised pointer = **wild** pointer; `int *p; *p = 5;` is undefined
- `int *p, q;` declares p as a pointer but q as a plain int
- Array name is a constant pointer (`a++` illegal) but a pointer parameter can be incremented
- NULL pointer dereference crashes (segmentation fault)

notes.md:
> **Syllabus:** Definition, notation, pointers and arrays, arrays of pointers, pointers and functions – call by value and call by reference, pointers to pointers

### Definition (of a pointer)
- **Means:** a variable that stores the **address** of another variable.
- **Key facts:** size is the same for every type (8 bytes on 64-bit, 4 on 32-bit, 2 in old 16-bit Turbo C); uses – call by reference, dynamic memory, arrays/strings, data structures (linked lists, trees).
- **Example:** `int x = 7; int *p = &x;` → p holds x's address.
- **Exam point:** an uninitialised pointer is a **wild** pointer; `NULL` points nowhere.

### Notation
- **Means:** the symbols used: `&` (address-of) and `*` (value-at / indirection; also used in declarations).
- **Key facts:** `*p` = value at p; `&*p` = p; `*&x` = x; `%p` prints an address; `p++` moves by sizeof(type).
- **Example:** `int x = 7, *p = &x; *p = 9; printf("%d", x);` → 9.
- **Exam point:** `int *p, q;` → only p is a pointer.

### Pointers and arrays
- **Means:** an array name acts as a constant pointer to its first element.
- **Key facts:** `a[i]` ≡ `*(a + i)` ≡ `*(i + a)` ≡ `i[a]`; `p = a;` allowed, `a = p;` / `a++` not; pointer difference gives element count.
- **Example:** `int a[] = {2, 4, 6}, *p = a; printf("%d %d", *(p + 1), *p + 1);` → 4 3.
- **Exam point:** `sizeof(a)` = whole array; `sizeof(p)` = 8.

### Arrays of pointers
- **Means:** an array whose elements are pointers: `int *ap[3];`
- **Key facts:** common for lists of strings: `char *days[] = {"Mon", "Tue", "Wed"};` (each element points to a string); differs from a pointer to an array `int (*pa)[3];`.
- **Example:** `printf("%s %c", days[1], *days[2]);` → Tue W
- **Exam point:** `argv` in `main(int argc, char *argv[])` is an array of pointers.

### Pointers and functions
- **Means:** passing pointers to functions, returning pointers, and pointers to functions.
- **Key facts:** passing `&x` lets the function change x; never return the address of a local variable; function pointer `int (*fp)(int, int) = add; fp(2, 3);`
- **Example:** `void reset(int *p) { *p = 0; }`
- **Exam point:** `int *f();` = function returning pointer; `int (*f)();` = pointer to function.

### Call by value
- **Means:** the function gets a **copy** of the argument.
- **Key facts:** changes to parameters are lost on return; safe; default in C.
- **Example:** `void sw(int a, int b) { int t = a; a = b; b = t; }` → `sw(x, y)` leaves x and y unchanged.
- **Exam point:** the classic "swap doesn't work" question.

### Call by reference
- **Means:** the function gets the **address**, so it changes the original.
- **Key facts:** declare pointer parameters, call with `&`; used to "return" several values.
- **Example:** `void sw(int *a, int *b) { int t = *a; *a = *b; *b = t; }` → `sw(&x, &y)` swaps.
- **Exam point:** scanf uses call by reference (`&x`).

### Pointers to pointers
- **Means:** a pointer that stores the address of another pointer: `int **pp`.
- **Key facts:** `**pp` reaches the original value; used for 2-D dynamic arrays, changing a pointer inside a function, `char **argv`.
- **Example:** `int x = 5, *p = &x, **pp = &p; **pp += 1; printf("%d", x);` → 6.
- **Exam point:** levels: `*pp` = p (an address), `**pp` = x (a value).

notes.md:
## Structures
- `struct student { int roll; char name[20]; };` defines a type (no memory) → `struct student s1, s[50];`
- Access: `s1.roll`; pointer `p->roll` = `(*p).roll` (`*p.x` means `*(p.x)`); arrays of structures `e[2].salary`; nested `v.in.y`
- Initialise `{3, 4}` (missing members 0); C99 designated `{.y = 5, .x = 2}`
- Assignment `s1 = s2` copies all members; `==` between structures is not allowed; strings: `strcpy(s.name, "Ravi")`
- Passed/returned by value (a copy) – pass a pointer for large structures
- sizeof may exceed the sum of members (padding): `{char c; int i;}` = 8; `{char a; char b; int c;}` = 8 vs `{char a; int c; char b;}` = 12
- Self-referential structure `struct node { int data; struct node *next; };` → linked lists

## Unions
- All members share one memory location; size = largest member (rounded up for alignment); one member valid at a time
- `union { int i; char c[4]; }` = 4; `union { int a[10]; char y; }` = 40; `{char a[10]; int b; double c;}` = 16
- Initialiser sets the first member; tagged union = struct { tag; union {...}; }

## typedef, enum, bit fields
- `typedef unsigned long ulong;` alias (no memory); `typedef char *String; String a, b;` → two pointers (but `#define String char *` → b is a char)
- `enum color { RED, GREEN, BLUE };` → 0, 1, 2; `enum { A = 5, B, C = 10, D }` → B = 6, D = 11; enumerators are int, may repeat values
- Bit fields: `unsigned int a : 3;` → 0…7; no `&`, no arrays of bit fields; values wrap (5 in 2 bits → 1); used for flags and hardware registers

notes.title: Structures and unions – detailed notes with worked examples
notes.md:
## Structure basics
```c
struct student {
    int roll;
    char name[20];
    float marks;
};
struct student s1 = {1, "Asha", 92.5f}, *ps = &s1;
printf("%d %s", s1.roll, ps->name);     /* 1 Asha */
```
- `ps->name` = `(*ps).name` (the brackets matter: `*ps.name` means `*(ps.name)`)
- Structures can be **assigned** (`s2 = s1;` copies every member, even arrays) but **not compared** with `==`
- `typedef struct student Student;` then `Student s;`
- Array of structures: `struct student cls[60];` → `cls[i].marks`
- Nested structures: `s.dob.year`; self-referential: `struct node { int data; struct node *next; };` (a member may be a pointer to its own type, not the type itself)

## Size and padding (64-bit GCC)
Each member is aligned to its own size; the total is rounded up to the largest alignment.
| Structure | sizeof | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| `{char c; int i; char d;}` | **12** | c + 3 pad, i, d + 3 pad |
| `{int i; char c; char d;}` | **8** | i, c, d + 2 pad |
| `{char a; char b; int c;}` | **8** | a, b + 2 pad, c |
| `{char c; double d;}` | **16** | c + 7 pad, d |
| `{char c; short s; int i;}` | **8** | c + 1 pad, s, i |
| `{int a[3]; char c;}` | **16** | 12 + 1 + 3 pad |
- Order members from largest to smallest to save space; `#pragma pack(1)` removes padding
- Exam questions without padding simply **add** member sizes – read the options

## Unions
- All members share **the same memory**; size = largest member rounded to the alignment
- Only one member holds a valid value at a time; writing one overwrites the others
| Union | sizeof |
|---|---|
| `{int i; char c;}` | 4 |
| `{int i; double d; char s[10];}` | **16** (10 rounded up to a multiple of 8) |
| `{char a[5]; int b;}` | 8 |
```c
union { int i; char c; } u;
u.i = 65;
printf("%c", u.c);            /* A – on a little-endian machine the low byte comes first */
union { int i; float f; } v;
v.f = 1.0f;                    /* v.i now holds the bit pattern 1065353216 (0x3F800000) */
```

| Structure | Union |
|---|---|
| separate memory for each member | shared memory |
| size ≥ sum of members | size = largest member |
| all members usable together | one at a time |
| keyword `struct` | keyword `union` |

## Bit fields
```c
struct flags { unsigned a : 1; unsigned b : 3; unsigned c : 4; };   /* sizeof = 4 */
```
- Width ≤ the type's bits; `&` cannot be applied to a bit field; `unsigned a : 1` holds 0 or 1

## enum
```c
enum color { RED, GREEN = 5, BLUE, WHITE = 2, BLACK };
/* RED = 0, GREEN = 5, BLUE = 6, WHITE = 2, BLACK = 3 */
```
- Each enumerator is the previous + 1 unless given; values may repeat; the type is int

## Passing structures to functions
- By value copies the whole structure (slow for large ones); pass a pointer (`void show(const struct student *p)`)
- A function may **return** a structure

## Traps
- A `;` is required after the closing `}` of a structure definition
- Members cannot be initialised inside the declaration in C (`struct s { int x = 5; };` is an error)
- `struct a { struct a x; };` is an error (infinite size); a pointer to `struct a` is fine
- Union size is **not** the sum of its members

notes.md:
> **Syllabus:** Structures – definition, declaration, accessing elements, arrays of structures, structure in a structure, pointers and structures; unions – definition, declaration, accessing elements; typedef, enum, bit fields

### Structures – definition
- **Means:** a user-defined type grouping variables of **different types** under one name.
- **Key facts:** keyword `struct`; members get separate memory; size ≥ sum of members (padding).
- **Example:** `struct book { char title[40]; float price; int pages; };`
- **Exam point:** definition ends with `};` and allocates **no memory** until a variable is declared.

### Declaration (of structure variables)
- **Means:** creating variables of the structure type.
- **Key facts:** `struct book b1, b2;` or together with the definition `struct book {…} b1;`; initialise `struct book b = {"C", 250.0, 300};`
- **Example:** `struct point { int x, y; } p = {3, 4};`
- **Exam point:** members cannot be initialised inside the definition.

### Accessing elements
- **Means:** reading/writing members with the dot operator `.`
- **Key facts:** `b1.price = 300;` ; `scanf("%d", &b1.pages);` ; strings: `strcpy(b1.title, "DS");` (not `b1.title = "DS"`).
- **Example:** `printf("%d", p.x + p.y);` → 7.
- **Exam point:** whole structures can be assigned (`b2 = b1`) but not compared (`b1 == b2` is an error).

### Arrays of structures
- **Means:** an array whose elements are structures – a table of records.
- **Key facts:** `struct student s[60];` → `s[i].marks`; loop over records.
- **Example:** `struct emp e[3]; for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) total += e[i].sal;`
- **Exam point:** `sizeof(s)` = 60 × sizeof(struct student).

### Structure in a structure (nested)
- **Means:** a member that is itself a structure.
- **Key facts:** access with two dots: `e.dob.year`; inner type defined before or inside.
- **Example:** `struct date { int d, m, y; }; struct emp { char name[20]; struct date dob; } e; e.dob.y = 1990;`
- **Exam point:** a structure cannot contain itself, only a pointer to itself.

### Pointers and structures
- **Means:** pointer variables that point to structures.
- **Key facts:** `struct book *pb = &b1;` access with arrow `pb->price` = `(*pb).price`; basis of linked lists (`struct node *next`); pass pointers to functions to avoid copying.
- **Example:** `pb->pages += 10;`
- **Exam point:** `*pb.price` is wrong (`.` binds tighter than `*`).

### Unions – definition
- **Means:** like a structure, but **all members share one memory location**.
- **Key facts:** keyword `union`; size = largest member (rounded for alignment); saves memory when only one member is needed at a time.
- **Example:** `union data { int i; float f; char s[8]; };` → sizeof = 8.
- **Exam point:** union size = max, structure size = sum (+ padding).

### Unions – declaration
- **Means:** creating union variables.
- **Key facts:** `union data d1;` ; only the **first member** can be initialised in C89: `union data d = {10};` (C99 designated: `{.f = 2.5}`).
- **Example:** `union data d = {65};`
- **Exam point:** declaring a union allocates memory for its largest member only.

### Unions – accessing elements
- **Means:** using `.` (or `->`) just like structures.
- **Key facts:** writing one member overwrites the others; read only the member last written.
- **Example:** `d.i = 65; d.f = 1.5; printf("%d", d.i);` → not 65 (the float overwrote it).
- **Exam point:** a union holds **one** valid value at a time.

### typedef
- **Means:** creates a new name (alias) for an existing type.
- **Key facts:** `typedef unsigned int uint;` · `typedef struct book Book;` · `typedef struct { int x, y; } Point;` – does not create a new type, just a name.
- **Example:** `Point p = {1, 2};`
- **Exam point:** typedef is handled by the compiler; `#define` by the preprocessor.

### enum
- **Means:** user-defined type of named integer constants.
- **Key facts:** starts at 0, each next +1 unless assigned; values may repeat.
- **Example:** `enum day { MON = 1, TUE, WED }; printf("%d", WED);` → 3.
- **Exam point:** `enum {A, B = 5, C};` → A 0, B 5, C 6.

### Bit fields
- **Means:** structure members with a specified number of **bits**.
- **Key facts:** `struct { unsigned on : 1; unsigned mode : 3; } f;` saves memory (flags, hardware registers); range of a 3-bit unsigned field 0–7; no `&` on a bit field; no arrays of bit fields.
- **Example:** `f.mode = 9;` stores 9 mod 8 = 1.
- **Exam point:** width cannot exceed the bits of the base type.

notes.title: Bitwise operators – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Operators
| Op | Name | Example (12 = 1100, 10 = 1010) |
|---|---|---|
| `&` | AND | 12 & 10 = 8 |
| `|` | OR | 12 | 10 = 14 |
| `^` | XOR | 12 ^ 10 = 6 |
| `~` | complement (unary) | ~5 = −6, ~0 = −1 |
| `<<` | left shift (× 2ⁿ) | 5 << 2 = 20 |
| `>>` | right shift (÷ 2ⁿ) | 100 >> 3 = 12 |
- Integer operands only; precedence: shifts < `+ -`; `&` > `^` > `|`, all below `==` (so `a & b == c` is `a & (b == c)`)
- `5 & 2` = 0 but `5 && 2` = 1; `7 & 3 | 8` = 11; `1 << 2 + 1` = 8; `(x << 1) + (x >> 1)` with x = 2 → 5

## Bit tricks
- Test odd: `n & 1`; bit k: `(x >> k) & 1`
- Set `x | (1 << k)`; clear `x & ~(1 << k)`; toggle `x ^ (1 << k)`
- Power of two: `(n & (n − 1)) == 0`; count 1 bits: `c += n & 1; n >>= 1;`
- Mask of k ones: `(1 << k) − 1`; low nibble `x & 0x0F`; swap nibbles `((x & 0x0F) << 4) | ((x & 0xF0) >> 4)`
- XOR swap `a ^= b; b ^= a; a ^= b;`; `x ^ x = 0`; `x ^ k ^ k = x`
- Right shift of a negative signed value is implementation-defined (usually arithmetic); shifting by ≥ width is undefined

notes.title: Bitwise operators – detailed notes with worked examples
notes.md:
## The six operators
| Op | Name | 12 op 10 (1100, 1010) |
|---|---|---|
| `&` | AND | 1000 = **8** |
| `\|` | OR | 1110 = **14** |
| `^` | XOR | 0110 = **6** |
| `~` | NOT (one's complement) | ~12 = **−13** (rule: ~x = −x − 1) |
| `<<` | left shift | 5 << 2 = **20** (× 2²) |
| `>>` | right shift | 20 >> 2 = **5** (÷ 2², truncating) |
- Work only on integer types (char, int, long …), not float/double
- `>>` on a negative number is implementation-defined (GCC does an arithmetic shift: −8 >> 1 = −4); on **unsigned** it fills with 0s
- Shifting by ≥ the width of the type, or a negative amount, is undefined

## Two's complement (how negatives are stored)
- −x = ~x + 1. In 8 bits: 5 = 00000101 → −5 = **11111011**
- Range of n-bit signed: −2ⁿ⁻¹ … 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1 (8 bits: −128 … 127)
- `printf("%d", ~0);` → −1; `printf("%u", ~0u);` → 4294967295

## Tricks every exam uses
| Task | Expression |
|---|---|
| Is x odd? | `x & 1` |
| Is x a power of 2? | `x && !(x & (x − 1))` |
| Set bit n | `x \| (1 << n)` |
| Clear bit n | `x & ~(1 << n)` |
| Toggle bit n | `x ^ (1 << n)` |
| Test bit n | `(x >> n) & 1` |
| Multiply / divide by 2ⁿ | `x << n`, `x >> n` |
| Swap without a temp | `a ^= b; b ^= a; a ^= b;` (fails if a and b are the same variable) |
| Turn off the lowest set bit | `x & (x − 1)` |
| Keep only the lowest set bit | `x & −x` |
| Count set bits (Kernighan) | `while (x) { x &= x − 1; c++; }` |
| Lower 4 bits | `x & 0x0F` |

## Output tracing
```c
int a = 7, b = 5;
printf("%d %d %d\n", a & b, a | b, a ^ b);   /* 5 7 2   (111 & 101, 111 | 101, 111 ^ 101) */
printf("%d %d\n", a << 1, a >> 1);            /* 14 3 */
printf("%d\n", ~a);                           /* -8  */
int x = 10;                                    /* 1010 */
x = x | (1 << 0);                              /* 1011 = 11 */
x = x & ~(1 << 3);                             /* 0011 = 3  */
printf("%d\n", x);                            /* 3 */
unsigned char c = 0xF0;
printf("%X\n", c >> 4);                       /* F */
printf("%d\n", 1 << 10);                      /* 1024 */
```

## XOR facts
- x ^ x = 0, x ^ 0 = x, XOR is commutative and associative
- The number that appears once among pairs: XOR all elements (2 ^ 3 ^ 2 = 3)
- Simple XOR encryption: c = m ^ k; m = c ^ k

## Logical vs bitwise
| | `&&` / `\|\|` | `&` / `\|` |
|---|---|---|
| Result | 0 or 1 | bit pattern |
| Short-circuit | yes | no (both sides evaluated) |
| 5 op 2 | 5 && 2 = 1 | 5 & 2 = 0 |

## Traps
- **Precedence**: `==` binds tighter than `&`, `^`, `|` → `if (x & 1 == 0)` means `x & (1 == 0)` = 0 → always false. Write `if ((x & 1) == 0)`
- `<<` binds looser than `+`: `1 << 2 + 1` = 1 << 3 = 8
- `~` on an unsigned char promotes to int first: `~(unsigned char)0` = −1 as int

notes.title: KRIES syllabus word by word – Bitwise operators
notes.md:
> **Syllabus:** Bitwise AND, OR, exclusive OR, complement, right shift and left shift operators

### Bitwise AND (`&`)
- **Means:** result bit is 1 only if **both** bits are 1.
- **Key facts:** used for **masking** (keep chosen bits), testing a bit, checking odd/even (`n & 1`).
- **Example:** 12 & 10 → 1100 & 1010 = 1000 = **8**; `0x2F & 0x0F` = 0x0F.
- **Exam point:** `&` (bitwise) ≠ `&&` (logical): 4 & 2 = 0 but 4 && 2 = 1.

### Bitwise OR (`|`)
- **Means:** result bit is 1 if **either** bit is 1.
- **Key facts:** used to **set** bits: `flags | (1 << n)`.
- **Example:** 12 | 10 → 1110 = **14**; 5 | 2 = 7.
- **Exam point:** x | 0 = x; x | x = x.

### Exclusive OR (`^`)
- **Means:** result bit is 1 if the bits are **different**.
- **Key facts:** x ^ x = 0, x ^ 0 = x; used to **toggle** bits, swap without a temporary, simple encryption, find the odd-one-out.
- **Example:** 12 ^ 10 → 0110 = **6**; a = 5, b = 9: a ^= b; b ^= a; a ^= b → a = 9, b = 5.
- **Exam point:** `^` is XOR, **not** power in C (use `pow`).

### Complement (`~`)
- **Means:** one's complement – flips every bit (unary).
- **Key facts:** for signed int, **~x = −(x + 1)**; for unsigned 8-bit, ~x = 255 − x.
- **Example:** ~5 = **−6**; ~0 = −1; `(unsigned char)~5` = 250.
- **Exam point:** two's complement = one's complement + 1 (that is how −x is stored).

### Right shift (`>>`)
- **Means:** moves bits right by n places.
- **Key facts:** x >> n = x ÷ 2ⁿ (integer); unsigned → zeros come in on the left; signed negative → implementation-defined (usually sign bit copied).
- **Example:** 40 >> 3 = **5**; 7 >> 1 = 3.
- **Exam point:** shifting by a negative count or ≥ the width is undefined.

### Left shift (`<<`)
- **Means:** moves bits left by n places, zeros fill on the right.
- **Key facts:** x << n = x × 2ⁿ (if no overflow); `1 << n` makes a mask with bit n set.
- **Example:** 5 << 2 = **20**; 1 << 4 = 16.
- **Exam point:** `<<`/`>>` have **lower** precedence than `+`/`-`: `1 << 2 + 1` = 1 << 3 = 8.

notes.title: C preprocessor – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Directives (start with #, no semicolon, processed before compilation)
| Type | Directives |
|---|---|
| Macro substitution | `#define`, `#undef` |
| File inclusion | `#include <file.h>` (system dirs), `#include "file.h"` (current dir first) |
| Conditional compilation | `#if`, `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#elif`, `#else`, `#endif`, `defined()` |
| Others | `#pragma`, `#error`, `#line` |
- Predefined: `__LINE__`, `__FILE__`, `__DATE__`, `__TIME__`, `__STDC__`
- Output of the preprocessor: .i file (gcc -E); comments removed; include guards `#ifndef X_H #define X_H … #endif` or `#pragma once`
- Headers: stdio.h (printf, FILE), stdlib.h (malloc, exit, atoi), string.h, math.h (sqrt, pow), ctype.h, conio.h (Turbo C only)

## Macros
- Object-like `#define PI 3.14`; function-like `#define SQ(x) ((x) * (x))`
- Pitfalls: `#define SQUARE(x) x * x` → SQUARE(2 + 3) = 11; `3 * DOUBLE(2)` with `x + x` = 8; `AREA(1 + 1)` with `3.14 * r * r` = 5.14
- `#define N 10;` puts the ; into the code; side effects (`SQR(i++)`) are evaluated twice
- `#x` stringizes, `a##b` pastes tokens; not replaced inside "strings"; continue lines with `\`
- Macro vs function: no call overhead, no type checking, bigger code; C99 `inline` functions are the safe alternative
- `gcc -DDEBUG` defines DEBUG on the command line

notes.title: C preprocessor – detailed notes with worked examples
notes.md:
## What it is
- Runs **before** compilation; lines start with `#`; no `;` at the end; `gcc -E file.c` shows its output
- Directives: `#include`, `#define`, `#undef`, `#if`, `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#elif`, `#else`, `#endif`, `#error`, `#pragma`, `#line`

## #include
- `#include <stdio.h>` – searches the system/include directories
- `#include "myhdr.h"` – searches the current directory first, then system directories
- Header files hold declarations (prototypes, macros, typedefs), not normally function bodies
- **Include guard** to stop double inclusion:
```c
#ifndef MYHDR_H
#define MYHDR_H
/* declarations */
#endif
```
(or `#pragma once`, non-standard but widely supported)

## Object-like and function-like macros
```c
#define PI 3.14159
#define MAX(a, b) ((a) > (b) ? (a) : (b))
```
Macros are **text substitution** – no type checking, no evaluation.

## Macro tracing – the most asked questions
| Macro | Use | Expands to | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#define SQ(x) x * x` | `SQ(3 + 2)` | `3 + 2 * 3 + 2` | **11** |
| `#define SQ(x) ((x) * (x))` | `SQ(3 + 2)` | `((3 + 2) * (3 + 2))` | **25** |
| `#define DBL(x) x + x` | `10 * DBL(2)` | `10 * 2 + 2` | **22** |
| `#define DBL(x) ((x) + (x))` | `10 * DBL(2)` | | **40** |
| `#define SQ(x) ((x) * (x))` | `100 / SQ(5)` | `100 / ((5) * (5))` | **4** |
| `#define SQ(x) x * x` | `100 / SQ(5)` | `100 / 5 * 5` | **100** |
| `#define CUBE(x) (x * x * x)` | `CUBE(1 + 1)` | `(1 + 1 * 1 + 1 * 1 + 1)` | **4** |
| `#define SQ(x) ((x) * (x))` | `SQ(i++)` | `((i++) * (i++))` | **undefined** (i changed twice) |
Rule: put brackets around **every parameter and the whole body**.

## # and ## operators
- `#` stringises: `#define STR(x) #x` → `STR(hello)` becomes `"hello"`
- `##` pastes tokens: `#define CAT(a, b) a##b` → `CAT(var, 1)` becomes `var1`
- Multi-line macro: end each line with `\`

## Predefined macros
`__FILE__` (file name), `__LINE__` (line number), `__DATE__`, `__TIME__`, `__STDC__` (1 if standard C), `__STDC_VERSION__`; C99's `__func__` is the current function name (an identifier, not a macro)
```c
printf("%s line %d", __FILE__, __LINE__);
```

## Conditional compilation
```c
#define DEBUG 1
#if DEBUG
    printf("x = %d\n", x);
#endif

#ifdef _WIN32
    /* Windows-only code */
#else
    /* other systems */
#endif
```
- Used for debugging switches, portability, include guards; `#undef PI` removes a definition

## Macro vs function
| Macro | Function |
|---|---|
| expanded inline – no call overhead (faster) | one copy of code – call overhead |
| code grows with each use | smaller code |
| no type checking | arguments type-checked |
| arguments may be evaluated twice | evaluated once |
| hard to debug | easy to debug |
| C99 alternative: `inline` functions | |
- `#define` vs `const`: a const variable has a type and scope and is visible to the debugger; a macro is just text

## Traps
- `#define PI 3.14;` (with a `;`) puts the `;` into every use → errors such as `area = PI * r * r;` becoming `3.14; * r * r`
- Macro names are not replaced inside string literals: `printf("PI")` prints PI
- A macro can be redefined only after `#undef` (or with an identical body)
- `#include` can include any file, even a .c file (bad practice)

notes.md:
> **Syllabus:** Types of C preprocessor directives, macros, file inclusion

### C preprocessor
- **Means:** a program that processes the source **before compilation** – handles lines starting with `#`.
- **Key facts:** removes comments, expands macros, includes files, compiles conditionally; directives end at the line end (no `;`); `gcc -E` shows its output.
- **Exam point:** preprocessing is the **first** stage of the build.

### Types of preprocessor directives
- **Means:** the kinds of `#` commands.
- **Key facts:** (1) **macro substitution** – `#define`, `#undef`; (2) **file inclusion** – `#include`; (3) **conditional compilation** – `#if`, `#ifdef`, `#ifndef`, `#elif`, `#else`, `#endif`; (4) **miscellaneous** – `#pragma`, `#error`, `#line`.
- **Example:** `#ifdef DEBUG printf("x=%d", x); #endif` – compiled only when DEBUG is defined.
- **Exam point:** `#pragma` gives compiler-specific instructions (`#pragma once`, `#pragma pack(1)`).

### Macros
- **Means:** names replaced by text before compiling – object-like (`#define PI 3.14`) and function-like (`#define SQ(x) ((x) * (x))`).
- **Key facts:** pure text substitution – no type checking; faster (no call) but bigger code; bracket every argument and the whole body; `#` stringises, `##` joins tokens; `#undef` removes.
- **Example:** `#define SQ(x) x * x` → `SQ(2 + 3)` = 2 + 3 * 2 + 3 = **11**; with brackets = 25.
- **Exam point:** `#define MAX 10;` (with `;`) breaks expressions where MAX is used.

### File inclusion
- **Means:** `#include` copies another file's contents into the program.
- **Key facts:** `#include <file.h>` searches standard directories; `#include "file.h"` searches the current directory first; header files hold prototypes, macros, typedefs; guard against double inclusion with `#ifndef X_H #define X_H … #endif`.
- **Example:** `#include <math.h>` gives `sqrt()`, `pow()`; `#include "myfuns.h"`.
- **Exam point:** including a header gives declarations; the library code itself is added by the **linker**.
